step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify the visual nodes drawn on the whiteboard:
   - On-premises database icon (OnPremDC)
   - Storage Gateway (StorageGateway)
   - Direct Connect (DirectConnect)
   - Landing S3 Bucket (S3)
   - Quality Cleansing EC2 node (EC2)
   - RDS database for metadata/scripts (RDS)
   - Transformation S3 Bucket (S3)
   - Transformation EC2 node (EC2)
   - Redshift (RedShift)
   - Publish S3 Bucket (S3)
   - Glacier Archival S3 Bucket (S3 - note: Glacier is mapped to S3 as per exact schema service list)
2. Identify visual edges following data flow direction:
   - OnPremDC -> StorageGateway -> DirectConnect -> Landing S3 Bucket
   - Landing S3 -> Quality Cleansing EC2
   - Quality Cleansing EC2 <-> RDS (for metadata/transformation scripts)
   - Quality Cleansing EC2 -> Transformation S3
   - Transformation S3 -> Transformation EC2
   - Transformation EC2 <-> RDS (metadata/scripts access)
   - Transformation EC2 -> RedShift
   - RedShift -> Publish S3
   - Publish S3 -> Glacier S3

graph.name: Capgemini On-Premises Netezza Migration to AWS Redshift
graph.notes: Architecture showing daily automated data ingestion from on-premises database via Storage Gateway and Direct Connect into S3 landing zone, ELT processing with EC2 and RDS metadata, loading into Redshift, publishing to S3 dashboard bucket, and archiving to Glacier.

nodes.name: Glacier Storage
nodes.notes: Long-term archive storage for publish bucket lifecycle

edges.notes: Daily data incremental extract from source DB
Ingestion data stream sent via Direct Connect
Data lands in S3 Landing Zone
Quality cleansing node picks up data from landing zone
Writes cleansed data to transformation bucket
Transforms and loads data into Redshift
Publishes data from Redshift to Publish S3 bucket
Lifecycle retention moves old data to Glacier archive
